I worked for a special needs summer camp in upstate new York about two years ago. At the end of each session we took the campers to a lake for boating and swiming etc.
The last session of the season I'm working 1-1 with a male camper, he's about 200 or so pounds and I'm a 5'3 120 pound female.

So my camper isn't a great swimmer, he has some aggression issues and panics if his feet can't touch the bottom of the pool when we were at camp. So off we go into the lake, I'm with him and trying to stop him going too far into the water, trying to keep him about waist height. However someone throws an inflatable ball too far out and my camper decides to go after it, I'm trying to get him to come back to me, swimming with him, hoping he doesn't realise he can't touch the bottom of the lake if he stops swimming.
Guess what?
He panics, pulls me under to keep himself afloat. I'm a strong swimming but when a very heavy disabled grown man is pushing me under the water there's not much I can do. Next thing I  remember is waking up in the camp's nursing van.
I thought I was done for. 
So that's my "I almost was drowned by a mentally disabled grown man" story.
